projects.title: TIDE-HF — Clinical Decision Support Platform for Congestive Heart Failure Management
projects.description: Built an end-to-end OLTP-to-OLAP healthcare data pipeline using Python, PostgreSQL, and dbt, automating cohort extraction across 546K+ clinical admissions, 60+ ICD codes, and 70+ laboratory analytes to produce a reproducible 137K-visit training dataset. Engineered 108 temporal features and trained 11 multi-label LightGBM models for clinical risk prediction, achieving 0.78–0.98 AUROC across hyperkalemia, AKI, and worsening-heart-failure prediction tasks. Developed a privacy-focused clinical decision-support application using FastAPI, Streamlit, ChromaDB, RAG, and MCP, integrating rule-based clinical recommendations and an XGBoost mortality-risk module with SHAP explainability. Implemented AWS S3-based cloud storage and data ingestion workflows to organize clinical datasets and support scalable processing across the analytics pipeline.

Developed a privacy-focused clinical decision-support application using FastAPI, Streamlit, ChromaDB, RAG, and MCP, integrating rule-based clinical recommendations and an XGBoost mortality-risk module with SHAP explainability. Implemented AWS S3-based cloud storage and data ingestion workflows to organize clinical datasets and support scalable processing across the analytics pipeline.

projects.title: E-Commerce Retail Analytics Database
projects.description: Built a Python/PostgreSQL data pipeline processing 100K+ orders and 3M geolocation records, implementing a normalized 3NF database model for structured retail analytics. Developed SQL transformations, joins, aggregations, and data validation logic to integrate order, customer, product, seller, and geolocation datasets into analytics-ready tables. Optimized SQL queries, indexes, and database structures, achieving 60% faster query execution and improving performance of analytical workloads.

projects.description: The Type 2 Diabetes (T2D) is a growing global health issue. Many people remain undiagnosed due to the absence of early symptoms.
